llm_r1_c1.rationale_en: Baseline standard QAOA with p=6, no pruning, and fixed linear ramp angles to establish the performance floor without optimization overhead.

llm_r1_c2.rationale_en: Leverages the continuous relaxation via warm-start initialization and mixer with constant angles to test if the prior knowledge alone improves success probability.

llm_r1_c3.rationale_en: Tests the effect of aggressive coupling pruning (keeping only 50% of ZZ mass) to allow deeper p=8 circuits, checking if removing weak couplings helps or hurts.

llm_r1_c4.rationale_en: Uses RMS scaling and COBYLA optimization with low CVaR alpha to focus on the best 10% of outcomes, testing if optimization significantly boosts success rate.

llm_r1_c5.rationale_en: Combines warm-start with moderate pruning and Nelder-Mead optimization to see if the hybrid approach outperforms pure uniform or pure warm-start baselines.

llm_r1_c6.rationale_en: Explores extreme pruning (30% mass) with deep p=8 and constant angles to test if a very sparse Hamiltonian representation is sufficient for high success probability.

llm_r1_c7.rationale_en: Tests warm-start initialization with the standard X mixer and a short ramp duration to see if the initial state bias is enough without the specialized warm mixer.

llm_r1_c8.rationale_en: Uses moderate pruning to fit p=6 with optimization, focusing on the top 5% of outcomes via CVaR to maximize the probability of finding a near-optimal feasible solution.

llm_r2_c1.rationale_en: Refine the best candidate (c5) by maximizing optimizer iterations to 59 and tightening CVaR to 0.1 to better focus on the top feasible solutions.

llm_r2_c2.rationale_en: Increase circuit depth to 8 layers with aggressive coupling pruning (mass 0.5) to allow more expressive mixing while keeping gate count low, using aggressive CVaR.

llm_r2_c3.rationale_en: Test if a shallower circuit (4 layers) with full couplings and Cobyla optimization can outperform deeper circuits by converging faster on the warm-start landscape.

llm_r2_c4.rationale_en: Test if RMS scaling of the Hamiltonian improves the optimizer's ability to navigate the energy landscape compared to max scaling.

llm_r2_c5.rationale_en: Lower the warm-start epsilon to 0.05 to allow the initial state to more closely match the continuous relaxation, potentially improving the starting point for the optimizer.

llm_r2_c6.rationale_en: Use a slightly higher coupling mass (0.6) with 8 layers to retain more problem structure while still allowing deep mixing, aiming for a balance between expressivity and gate count.

llm_r2_c7.rationale_en: Compare Cobyla against Nelder-Mead on the same high-performing configuration to determine which optimizer is more effective for this specific QUBO structure.

llm_r2_c8.rationale_en: Test the extreme case of a single layer with full optimization to see if the warm-start state is already so good that minimal mixing is sufficient.
